key_insight: Learning-guided search discovers new extremal geometric constructions, improving the integrality-gap lower bound for stabbing unit squares beyond 3/2.
engineering_relevance: Combining machine learning with domain expertise can generate stronger stress tests for optimization relaxations and geometric algorithms.
method: Adapt PatternBoost via Axplorer to alternate local search with transformer-generated candidates.
Tailor representations, search operations, and surrogate ranking before exact verification.
Introduce expert-designed staircase seeds to diversify search and overcome plateaus.
evidence_signal: Across three geometric problems, tailored search found non-trivial constructions; for unit-square stabbing, automated search reached 20/13 ≈ 1.538, while expert-seeded search reached 14/9 ≈ 1.556.
watch_item: Naive representations failed, and automated search plateaued, indicating sensitivity to problem-specific design and initial-instance diversity.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
